item.title: Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.13841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Cao, Jan Palczewski

item.title: Asian option valuation under price impact
item.description: arXiv:2512.07154v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a model for arithmetic and geometric Asian option valuation with external order flow and dealer execution costs. We first formulate it as a discrete model and then obtain its continuous time scaling limit. We derive an explicit geometric Asian option formula under a consistent price system and formulate the dealer's bid and ask through utility indifference with constrained stock trading. We identify sufficient conditions for finite reservation prices and prove absence of arbitrage under the dealer's stock trading rules. Increasing initial inventory lowers both the reservation bid and the ask in the cases studied. In the finite-step calculations, higher temporary costs and greater risk aversion widen the spread for both payoffs, with a smaller change in the midpoint of the quotes.
item.dc:creator: Priyanshu Tiwari, Sourav Majumdar
